dishes.pitch: Let Copilot pick the right models for each prompt, then see which models answered.
about: Turn on Copilot Fusion in the Copilot app
Compare the execution patterns that Fusion uses
See which models answered your prompt
dishes.story: In this lab, you'll learn about Copilot Fusion by asking Copilot itself to explain it. Then you'll see which models teamed up to write your answer.

steps.body: In the taskbar, click the **GitHub Copilot app** icon to open it.
On the left, find **Sessions**. Click **+** (New) on the right.
steps.alt: The Sessions row in the Copilot app sidebar, with the New button on the right

steps.body: In the chat box, click the model name. Turn on **Copilot Fusion**. Under **Effort level**, select **High**.
steps.alt: The model menu in the chat box, with Copilot Fusion turned on and High selected under Effort level

steps.body: Copy this prompt and paste it into the chat.
steps.prompt: Read https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/models/copilot-fusion. What is Copilot Fusion, and what execution patterns can it use?

steps.body: Copy this prompt and paste it into the same chat.
steps.prompt: What is the difference between cascade and critique?

steps.body: Below the reply, find **Copilot Fusion** and the name of the model that answered. Then return here and click **I'm ready for the quiz**.
steps.alt: The label below a reply in the Copilot app that reads Copilot Fusion, GPT-6.1 Terra

quiz.question: What is Copilot Fusion?
quiz.answer: A model router and orchestrator that picks the models and pattern for each task
others: A new model that GitHub trained on code
A setting that makes one model reply faster
A tool that merges replies from chats you pick
quiz.hint: Read the reply to your first prompt.

quiz.question: Which pattern sends a draft to a judge that can escalate to a stronger model?
others: Single
Critique
Fusion Max
quiz.hint: Read the reply to your second prompt.

quiz.question: In the critique pattern, what happens after one model writes a draft?
quiz.answer: Several models review it, then the first model revises it
others: A judge accepts it or sends it to a stronger model
The fastest model rewrites it from the start
You pick the best draft from a list
quiz.hint: Read the reply to your second prompt.

wrap_up: In the Copilot app, delete the chat you used for this lab.

bullets: Many models work on one prompt
Effort levels to fit the task

dishes.pitch: Explore how you can give an agent its own tool with code.
about: Read an app that runs an agent
Find the tool the app gives the agent
Find how the app sends a prompt to the agent
dishes.story: In this lab, you'll explore a small Python app that uses the Microsoft Copilot SDK to run an agent. You'll use GitHub Copilot to understand how the app gives its agent a custom tool of its own.

steps.body: Click **Open in VS Code**. The starter opens with `main.py` showing.
Find **Copilot Chat** on the right side of VS Code. If you do not see it, press **Ctrl+Alt+I**.
Copy this question and paste it into the chat. Then find `get_menu` in `main.py`.
Copy this question and paste it into the chat. Then find `main` in `main.py`.
steps.prompt: How does the agent get the menu?

steps.body: In VS Code, open a terminal. Paste this command and press Enter.

quiz.question: How do you give the agent a custom tool?
quiz.answer: Decorate a function with `define_tool`, then pass it in `tools=[...]`
others: Describe the function in the prompt, then ask the agent to call it
Install it as a VS Code extension, then enable it in Copilot Chat
Name the function `tool_menu`, then import it in `main.py`
quiz.hint: Look at the line above `get_menu`, and at `create_session`.

quiz.question: A guest is vegetarian. How does the agent get only the vegetarian dishes?
quiz.answer: It calls `get_menu` with `vegetarian_only` set to true
others: It removes the meat dishes from its reply
It reads a vegetarian menu file
The prompt lists the vegetarian dishes
quiz.hint: Read the reply to your second question.

quiz.question: Which call sends a prompt and waits for the reply?
others: `create_session`
`define_tool`
`asyncio.run`
quiz.hint: Find the line that asks the vegetarian question.

bullets: Add an agent to your own app
Give it tools from your own code
Powered by the engine behind Copilot
receipt.tip: Give your app a Copilot of its own

dishes.pitch: Read a CI workflow where an agent triages issues every week.
about: How the frontmatter sets triggers, permissions and other settings
How the workflow gives the agent its instructions
How the workflow sets guardrails for the agent
dishes.story: In this lab, you'll explore a real agentic workflow: a GitHub Actions workflow written in Markdown. It puts an agent to work for the maintainers of a busy workshop repository. You'll find out when the agent runs, what its job is, and how the workflow keeps it safe.

steps.body: The frontmatter is the settings block at the top, between the `---` lines. Click **Open frontmatter** and find these keys:
details: `permissions:` sets what the workflow can access.
`safe-outputs:` sets what the workflow may change.

steps.body: The instructions are the plain-language prompt below the frontmatter. Click **Open instructions**. Read **What to do**. It gives the agent its job on each run.
In the same instructions, find these sections:
details: **Never close these** lists the items the agent must skip.
**When in doubt** tells the agent what to do when it is unsure.

quiz.question: When does the workflow run?
quiz.answer: Every Monday on a schedule, or manually on demand
others: Whenever a new issue or pull request is opened
On every push to `main`, or when a pull request is merged
Once a day at midnight, or when a maintainer adds a label
quiz.hint: Read the `on:` section at the top of the frontmatter.

quiz.question: Which items must the agent never close?
others: Items from first-time contributors
Items that are older than one week
Items that have no labels

quiz.question: What does the agent do when it is unsure about an item?
others: Closes it with a polite comment
Adds a label for a maintainer
Asks the author a question
quiz.hint: Search the instructions for "When in doubt".

wrap_up: Close the browser tabs you opened.

bullets: Add an agent to your automations
Runs on a schedule or on repo events
Safe and secure on GitHub Actions

dishes.pitch: See how AI reviewers catch bugs in a pull request.
about: Review the fix from Copilot Autofix
Review all suggestions from Copilot code review
dishes.story: In this lab, you'll review a pull request that sneaks a security vulnerability into our code. You'll watch GitHub Advanced Security catch it, then see what else Copilot code review finds.

steps.text: Find the issue with GitHub Advanced Security
steps.body: In the pull request, find the **github-advanced-security** comment:
details: **CodeQL / Database query built from user-controlled sources** names the issue.
The **code above the comment** is the flagged line.
**Suggested changeset** is the fix from Copilot Autofix. Red is unsafe. Green is fixed.

steps.text: Find the same issue in Copilot code review
steps.body: Scroll down to the **Copilot** review. Find the comment about the same query. Read the risk and the fix it suggests.
Read **Register the search route before the parameterized ID route**. Read why Copilot thinks the search route never runs.

quiz.question: What type of issue did code scanning find?
others: Exposed secret
Outdated dependency
Cross site scripting
quiz.hint: User input ends up inside a database query.

quiz.question: What fix did Copilot Autofix suggest?
quiz.answer: Pass the search term as a query parameter
others: Remove the search route
Escape quotes in the search term
Limit the length of the search term
quiz.hint: Compare the red and green lines in Suggested changeset.

quiz.question: Code scanning finds security vulnerabilities. What else does Copilot code review find?
others: Only security vulnerabilities
Outdated dependencies
Exposed secrets
quiz.hint: Read why the search route never runs.

wrap_up: Close the browser tabs you opened.

bullets: Copilot code review checks your PRs
receipt.tip: Ask Copilot to review your next PR
